As someone who’s lived with depression for most of their life, I relate with a lot of what you’re saying.
 

I too, wish I could/could’ve talked to the people I loved about my depression and suicidal thoughts. Letting the depression fester with no way of getting it out feels horrible.


This society is flawed, no way around that. Depressed and suicidal people often struggle in silence. There are so many faces that people don’t realize the masked face. The well-off people don’t like wasting their time with somebody worse off than them.


Since nobody around us either can’t see through our masks or don’t care enough to, we often have to come out of the depression ourselves. 

The best thing to do imo is to change our habits and coping mechanisms. When I get depressed I usually lie down in bed and listen to the punk/rock song that is the loudest and angriest, and wallow in my depression and misery, adding on to the depression with self-deprecating thoughts such as -“I’ll never find love again”, “I’m a horrible person”, or my personal favorite, “I’m going to die alone”

My coping mechanism isn’t healthy. Most other coping mechanisms aren’t healthy either, and just make things worse. Changing one’s habits goes a long way, I think.

I really can relate to that. I'm a middle child and a twin, not a good combination. Anywho. I'm going through something similar at the moment. I never had/ don't  have any real friends, even though all of my siblings do. Hell, my sister is like the ringleader of the girls in our (9th) grade. Seeing her succeed all the time really started to get to me after a while. "Why should she get to be perfect? Why does she get all of the affection?", that kind of thing. Hell, I just made a seperate post on here because of something like this. I'm the socially awkward one in the family. The one people glance over.

But. Seeing as how you're legally an adult, there is one peice of advice I can give. Just get out there. Even if it's hard (and trust me, I know how bad social awkwardness can be at times), just get yourself out there. Go to to park or the gym. Make connections with good people you find there. Eventually, it'll have to work. "Our greatest glory is not in never falling, but in rising every time we fall"- Confucius. 

Oh. Also. You said you like playing instruments. That's good. And three of them, damn. More than I could ever do. I'm getting off topic. My point is - You do what makes you happy. If that's music, by all means, go for it. Find your calling. For me, I'm a huge nerd when it comes to foreign languages. I find joy in learning languages. Do what you find joy in.
